PullRequest.Title: sessions: avoid permission picker flash
PullRequest.Body:

## Description

Prevents running-session mode and permission controls from briefly rendering below the chat input before moving into the input when `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` is enabled.

The Sessions chat view now initializes a scoped effective-layout context key before constructing the shared chat widget. Running-session picker contributions consume that key instead of global configuration context keys, which can briefly expose their defaults while the input is created. A regression test verifies the scoped layout wins even when the global configuration keys still contain the opposite values.

## Validation

- Passed: `npm run transpile-client`
- Passed: `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/common/contextkeys.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chatView.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.test.ts`
- Passed: `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.test.ts --grep \"places running session controls from the scoped composer layout|places mode immediately\"`
- Manual OSS check: launched with both experimental composer settings forced on; the new-session composer rendered the permission control directly in its input toolbar.
- Blocked before source compilation: `npm run compile-client` reports the existing runtime mismatch: `package.json` declares `1.0.90`, while `@github/copilot-sdk` bundles `1.0.89-7`.
- The full config-picker test file otherwise passed 50 tests and reproduced one unrelated existing failure in `keeps isolation picker focus and blocks changes while config resolves` (actual `pointerEvents: auto`, expected `none`).

> **Stacked PR:** This change is based on #339110. The custom-background CSS and screenshot changes visible in the aggregate diff are owned and reviewed there; this PR adds only the composer initialization fix on top.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a running Sessions chat view with the experimental composer enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The constructor computes two configuration values plus phone layout, binds and sets one scoped context key before creating ChatWidget, and ChatInputPart creates the primary toolbar. The diff skips creation and initial responsive layout of the secondary MenuWorkbenchToolBar; no new asynchronous operation gates rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the active agent-host session state through the existing AgentHostGenericConfigChips lane
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active session-state subscription per rendered chat input; identity checks reuse it for the same session/connection, independent of the four menu picker actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same generic-chip lane was instantiated, rendered, and attached before the PR because it sits outside the newly guarded secondary-toolbar block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Subscription attachment occurs during input construction, but it was already present before this diff and is not multiplied by suppressing the secondary toolbar.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve initial session configuration for a local untitled session lacking a provisional backend
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one current resolve attempt per input/session state, with replacement cancellation and an initial-result guard; this is not one call per picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This async resolve was reached from the same always-created generic-chip lane before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promise is launched without awaiting it, so it is off the initial render critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of simultaneously rendered ChatView instances, not transcript size or number of sessions in history. Picker action cardinality is fixed at four, and the PR removes one toolbar/listener/responsive-layout instance per experimental view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All changed context-key, menu, and DOM setup is synchronous per view. Existing agent-host subscriptions may exist once per live input; the diff adds no burst, queue, or parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Context writes are equality-checked and do not emit on the immediate repeated assignment. Existing generic-chip resolution retains only the current session result/subscription and replaces it on session changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed option directly guards MenuWorkbenchToolBar creation, its menu listeners, and secondary responsive-layout construction; repository code shows no new boundary inside the changed path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of concurrently rendered split views varies, but the changed work is constant per view and is a net reduction in experimental mode.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added scoped boolean is constant-cost and lifecycle-owned, while experimental view startup performs less synchronous UI construction than before.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change either experimental composer setting or switch between phone and desktop layout while a Sessions chat view is alive
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only the two relevant configuration keys and IsPhoneLayoutContext invoke updateExperimentalComposerLayout. The handler recomputes three booleans, equality-sets the scoped context key, toggles one class, and repositions/sizes existing input UI synchronously.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One handler invocation per affected setting/layout event per live ChatView. Menu reevaluation is bounded to context-dependent actions for that scoped input; no transcript or session collection is traversed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are handled synchronously on the UI thread with no subprocess, filesystem, database, network, or IPC call. ContextKeyService suppresses unchanged values, so unrelated or duplicate effective states do not fan out menu updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current context value acts as equality-deduplicated state; there are no cold/warm remote reads or negative-cache states on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both listener filters and ContextKeyService equality suppression are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual setting and responsive-layout toggle frequency is user/environment dependent but normally low, and multiplicity is bounded by live views.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Before the PR, global configuration/phone context expressions also drove toolbar menu updates; the scoped key does not increase realistic event cardinality or add an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create ordinary shared ChatWidget surfaces or a Sessions view using the legacy composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatWidget forwards renderSecondaryToolbar with a default of true. Legacy and non-session widgets therefore retain the previous toolbar construction and responsive layout; Sessions adds only one scoped key allocation/set before widget construction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant additional context state per live Sessions ChatView; other ChatWidget surfaces retain their previous behavior exactly.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-widget setup only; no changed asynchronous work or concurrency control.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. The scoped context is disposed with ChatView, preventing lifetime growth across closed views.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default-true plumbing and registered scoped service establish both behavior preservation and cleanup ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The count of open widgets varies, but each holds one boolean context entry and no unbounded collection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing toolbar work is preserved where required, and the new scoped state is bounded and disposed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced view startup, runtime setting/layout changes, shared-widget defaults, context-key invalidation, menu/DOM construction, responsive layout, disposal, and the unchanged transitive agent-host IPC paths. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue was found.
